newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian gov't delays sale of electric company.
newsitem.headline: Colombian gov't delays sale of electric company.

text.p: BOGOTA, April 14 Reuter - Colombia's government decided to delay the sale of its 56.7 percent stake in the leading power company in southwest Colombia and to raise its minimum price-tag for the deal by $50 million, the Finance Ministry said.

Clemente del Valle, the ministry's chief of Public Credit, said the one-month delay, setting a new sale date of May 18, was caused by mostly bureaucratic problems that prevented the government from providing prospective buyers with complete information about Empresa de Energia del Pacifico on a timely basis EPSA.
He said revised calculations of electrical distribution rates and commercialization costs had also prompted the government to hike the minimum value of its stake in the company by $50 million.
Sources close to the privatization deal said the increase would put the cost of the government's stake in EPSA at about $520 million.
Chilean electric giant Endesa is among potential bidders for the government's controlling share in EPSA, but it objected just last week to any moves to raise the government's minimum selling price.

"I'm sure that it you were to ask each and everyone of the potential buyers none of them would say that they liked the idea of the minimum price going up. But what we're doing is in the interest of making the process as objective and transparent as possible," Del Valle said.

EPSA, which has an installed capacity of nearly 900 megawatts, generates and distributes electrical power in southwest Valle de Cauca province, one of Colombia's leading industrial hubs and an area seen as having enormous growth potential.
